messages.subject: Suggestion: data handling and cache with rOpenGov packages
messages.subject_clean: Suggestion: data handling and cache with rOpenGov packages
messages.body_plain:
Dear rOpenGov development list,

many rOpenGov packages retrieve data from original sources. The download may be slow, and the original data sources may change with time.

Therefore my suggestion (based on discussions with other developers) is that by default all data downloaded by rOpenGov packages would be cached and stored on a local folder.

This will speed up processing and help with documentation as a copy of the original data at the time of the analysis will be stored.

How to do this in practice? We have at least four distinct cases with data downloads:

1) API (e.g. http://github.com/ropengov/sotkanet/)
2) zips (e.g. http://github.com/ropengov/helsinki/pkg/R/HKK.R)
3) Individual files (some useful KML- and CSV-files are available from the Finnish authorities, for instance without proper API)
4) File groups (e.g. Statistics Finland provides ~3000 data sets as individual PX/CSV/XML files through the same portal)

API requests are a separate case, where my suggestion is that not all queries will be stored on a local file. Instead, the user may write down the access date if s/he needs this for documentation purposes.

The points 2-4 require download of a complete data set. The user should be able to define the download folder. If not given, a temporary folder will be created. After the initial download, the cached data will be used to speed up processing.

One example of cacheing is here: https://github.com/QBRC/RODProt/blob/master/R/get-resource.R If you have other useful tips, feel free to contribute links.

This is what I am planning to implement for rOpenGov packages that I maintain. Would be good to have a consensus on the default procedure, so your feedback is welcome, if any.

Leo

messages.subject: rOpenGov harmonized API calls?
messages.body_plain:
Many have agreed it would be useful to have a harmonized API calls for related rOpenGov packages, for instance based on S4 classes. Although these are more laborious to implement, time is scarce, and coordination across package developers might be a challenge.

Anyway, some thoughts to start with (based on Joona's earlier suggestion).

1) Datamart

Datamart provides an example.
http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/datamart/index.html
http://factbased.blogspot.fi/2012/06/a-wrapper-for-r-data-function.html

This would work as follows:

> library(helsinki)
> hel <- helsinki()
> queries(hel)
[1] "AddressList" "HSY" "DistrictBoundaries"
> addr <- query(hel, "AddressList")

A related (imaginary) package stockholm:

> library(stockholm)
> stk <- stockholm()
> queries(stk)
[1] "AddressList" "ZIPcodes"
> zip.codes <- query(stk, "ZIPcodes")

This demonstrates the advantages of a proper API. It is not clear whether Datamart itself is ready, so we should be cautious when considering their practices. Is it realistic to assume we have the resources to implement this sort of system? Perhaps we should just start with the option below, and make small-scale experimentation with datamart-type queries with specific packages (for instance between Finland + Sweden + Austria election data packages?) and see how it works there.

2) There is also a simple, alternative option without harmonized API that we have used so far in some packages:

GetSomeData("resource_name_or_url", local.dir = "~/tmp/", overwrite = FALSE)

This would download the original data in the local folder. If the data has been retrieved already, the local copy will be used instead (helping with speed & documentation issues). This is much easier to implement, but more complicated for a regular user since the user needs to keep track on correct resource names etc. and these may differ between countries for instance. Unless we stay strict in harmonizing naming conventions across independent packages (a challenge in itself).

For each package it would also be good to have an additional function that lists all data resources that are available through that package. At the moment I am handling this by giving comprehensive list of examples in the Rmd vignette. But perhaps we will also need a separate function that provides a listing (?)

My suggestion is to start with option 2 to get things forward and packages ready for CRAN. We can then think Datamart-type solutions in a longer term with those who are interested in the implementation work and able to use their time for that.

Leo
